Subject: Discovery notes and next steps — Redwood x CloudDocs

Hi Olivia (and team),

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page: 

What we heard from CloudDocs
- Goal: reduce per-file OCR cost and speed up document search relevance for historic archives (~120M documents).
- Current pain: high latency in search indexing, low recall on short-form queries, and unpredictable inference costs on bursts.
- Success metric: 20–30% cost reduction per query and median search latency < 150ms for common queries.

Redwood fit / proposed pilot
- Pilot: 2-week POC using Redwood-hosted inference with batch ingestion of a 500k-doc subset + embedding-based reranking.
- Deliverables: baseline latency/cost, qualitative relevance evaluation (3 prompt sets), and a recommended serving config (batching + quantization profile).

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Do you have a preferred 500k-doc subset we can use, or should we pull a representative sample?
2) Any compliance constraints (redaction/PII removal) we should know for the POC datasets?
3) Expected internal stakeholders for a technical kickoff (SEs, infra, product)?

Next steps
- Proposed date for technical kickoff: week of Aug 24 — can we lock a 45m slot?
- I'll prepare a one-pager with scope and acceptance criteria (attached).

Attachments:
- CloudDocs-discovery-notes.pdf (summary & acceptance criteria)

Thanks — I’ll hold a tentative kickoff slot Tue 8/25 11am PT unless you want a different time.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Subject: Re: Internal: CloudDocs — no response, propose re-engage plan

Stephanie / team,

Thanks for the context — high level thoughts from SE:
- Minimal sample: ~200k documents (PDFs + extracted text) with file-level metadata (created_at, doc_type, language). That will be enough to exercise indexing + reranking without the full dataset.
- Red flags: heavy PII without clear redaction rules, encrypted blobs we can’t access, or documents requiring special parsers (scanned images with non-standard layouts).

Proposed technical play for re-engage email:
- Short hook: "We ran a lightweight sample against Redwood for customers like X and saw 25% faster search recall at 60% lower per-query cost."
- Call ask: 30m technical sync (SE + infra) to confirm sample and POC success criteria.
- Demo ask: Offer a targeted demo that shows search latency comparisons and a quick walkthrough of embedding+rerank.

I put together a 1-page re-engage playbook and a demo outline (attached). If you’re happy with the messaging I can draft the demo script and an SE-friendly checklist.

Attachments:
- reengage-playbook.docx
